visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Shares traded at €8 before any rumours and closed at €9.50 yesterday. The offer is €10. What's the premium?
questions.explain: Measure against the undisturbed price: 10 ÷ 8 − 1 = 25%. Against €9.50, already lifted by the rumours, you'd get about 5%.

questions.q: An offer values the equity at €1bn. Net debt is €500m and EBITDA is €150m. What multiple of EBITDA is the buyer paying?
questions.explain: EBITDA belongs to lenders and shareholders, so divide enterprise value: 1,000 + 500 = 1,500, over 150 is 10x. Dividing equity value gives 6.7x.
questions.explain_at: One billion is the equity value

questions.q: A fund pays €1bn for the shares, repays €500m of existing debt and borrows €900m. How much equity does it put in?
questions.explain: Uses are €1.5bn: the shares plus the debt repaid. Take off €900m of new debt and the equity is €600m.

questions.q: A bidder ends its offer with 75% of an Italian listed company. How does it usually take the company private?

options.text: A merger into the unlisted bidder
They delist it at seventy-five percent
A decision by the target's board
A request to Consob to suspend it

questions.explain: Automatic delisting needs 90%. Below that, the target merges into the unlisted bidder by a shareholder vote, and those who don't approve can withdraw for cash.
questions.explain_at: the route is a merger of Recordati into the unlisted bidder

questions.q: GE Vernova pays 13x EBITDA for Trench. Why does that make the price look lower than it is?

options.text: It's based on equity value, not EV
It's on EBITDA two years ahead
It's on revenue, not on EBITDA

questions.explain: The 13x is on expected 2028 EBITDA, before synergies. On this year's numbers, with Marco's margin assumption, it's about 18x.
questions.explain_at: The thirteen times is on EBITDA for twenty twenty-eight
